news.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
news.title_en: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users

inline_images.caption: OpenRouter's email warns affected users that third parties may have read their requests to MiniMax models. | Image: Jonathan Kemper
inline_images.caption_en: OpenRouter's email warns affected users that third parties may have read their requests to MiniMax models. | Image: Jonathan Kemper

news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
Security researchers at Dragos sent roughly 2 million AI requests containing fake credentials to AI providers and uncovered major security flaws.

The researchers ran the tests from July through November 2026 and identified at least three compromised providers where attackers were actively stealing user data. None of the three knew they had been compromised until Dragos notified them.

Attackers in the largest incident harvested hundreds of AWS keys, including some from requests the provider had
news.summary_en: Security firm Dragos revealed between July and November 2026 that multiple AI inference providers failed to uphold data retention policies, leading to the theft of AWS keys and sensitive user requests. Investigations confirmed that some marketplace resellers enabled logging to intercept data, with instances of leaked test URLs being accessed within minutes from Beijing and Shanghai via internal communication platforms.
paragraphs: Security researchers at Dragos sent roughly 2 million AI requests containing fake credentials to AI providers and uncovered major security flaws.

The researchers ran the tests from July through November 2026 and identified at least three compromised providers where attackers were actively stealing user data. None of the three knew they had been compromised until Dragos notified them.

Attackers in the largest incident harvested hundreds of AWS keys, including some from requests the provider had rejected before processing. In some cases, they tested the stolen keys within hours, searched S3 storage, and tried to establish persistent access. One attacker also used ARTEX, an AI-powered attack tool.

Marketplace resellers read customer requests too. They didn't need to exploit a vulnerability, Dragos says, because listing a model at the lowest price and turning on logging was enough. In one case, someone on a residential internet connection in France tried to log in over SSH using passwords pulled from intercepted requests.

Privacy settings like "Zero Data Retention"(ZDR) were frequently ignored. Dragos says a Chinese AI lab accessed the secret test URLs in more than half of all requests, even when those requests went through US providers.

Even major US providers broke their own policies. One was still crawling a test URL more than two months after a single request. In another case, a secret test link showed up in an internal chat on Feishu (known outside China as Lark) 24 days after the request. The link was opened within two minutes on three computers and three phones in Beijing and Shanghai.

OpenRouter responded by removing three providers from its platform and revoking ZDR approval for 125 endpoints, partly because of the research findings and partly as a precaution. The company also emailed affected users, warning that third parties may have read requests sent to MiniMax models.
Affected providers, including Novita, Phala, and Together, have published preliminary security reports on the incident, though not all have done so yet.
### Intermediaries are the weak link

AI routers like OpenRouter give users a single API for models from different companies. Requests are routed to a pool of providers, sometimes across several hops, and Dragos says each hop can read the entire request and response.

Some of these routers operate as open marketplaces where the cheapest provider gets the traffic. In this case, providers including Novita, AtlasCloud, and StreamLake sat between OpenRouter and model developer MiniMax. Together runs its own infrastructure, and Phala has its roots in Web3.

Dragos warns companies against sending requests containing credentials to intermediaries. The researchers recommend that organizations control how their AI requests are routed, check their privacy settings, and plant their own canary tokens, fake credentials that give themselves away as soon as someone uses them.
news.title_zh: AI推理平台安全漏洞致用户密钥遭大规模窃取
news.summary_zh: 安全机构Dragos通过模拟测试发现，多家AI推理代理商存在严重的隐私泄露与密钥窃取漏洞，导致用户凭证遭到非法访问与持久化攻击
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】安全机构Dragos、AI路由服务商OpenRouter、推理平台Novita、Phala、Together及部分未公开第三方在全球性AI模型推理调用API接口及在线算力市场：通过向代理商投喂诱饵数据，揭露了攻击者窃取API密钥、滥用零数据留存政策以及利用内部日志泄露敏感信息的行为
【起因与机理】AI推理市场缺乏统一的端到端加密与安全合规标准，中间商为压低价格牺牲了数据隔离与安全合规性
【关键数据与实测】关键时间节点与后续：OpenRouter已紧急移除违规供应商并撤销125个终端的ZDR认证，受影响厂商正陆续发布初步安全报告。
【涉及范围与推进】核心涉案与合规细节：包括Novita、Phala及Together在内的多家服务商被指出无视“零数据留存”承诺，且存在长期的凭证日志残留。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Dragos (security researchers), OpenRouter, inference providers like Novita, Phala, and Together: Exposure of widespread API key theft, violation of 'Zero Data Retention' (ZDR) policies, and exploitation of internal logging mechanisms
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Lack of standardized end-to-end encryption in the fragmented AI inference supply chain and excessive cost-cutting by marketplace resellers
[Regulatory & Investigation Focus] Core Investigation & Findings: Dragos identified systemic data interception and credential theft, urging stricter oversight of AI middleware providers.
[Key Position & Outlook] Outlook & Timeline: OpenRouter removed non-compliant providers and revoked 125 ZDR certifications, with affected firms currently issuing security remediations.

news.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
news.title_en: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
news.author: Matthias Bastian
news.content_snippet:
The Lean and Mathlib community has confirmed that Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct. "We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement,"the community said in a statement.

news.summary_en: Stanford mathematician Levent Alpöge published a proof of the Riemann hypothesis on November 20, 2026, consisting of 17 million lines of Lean code. The Lean and Mathlib community confirmed the proof's correctness through independent execution and formal verification, officially resolving the century-old mathematical challenge.
paragraphs: The Lean and Mathlib community has confirmed that Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct. "We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement,"the community said in a statement.

Alpöge, a Stanford mathematician, published the proof on Nov. 20, 2026, as 17 million lines of code written in Lean, a tool that checks mathematical proofs for errors. Dozens of people ran the code independently and got the same result. The verification programs are designed so they provably cannot accept a flawed proof. MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland lists the independent checks on his website.

The Riemann hypothesis had been one of the most famous unsolved problems in math, making a prediction about how prime numbers are distributed. The video below, generated with Fable 5.2, explains the proof if you want to dig deeper.

The solution arrived much earlier than expected. As Ethan Mollick notes, forecasters on Metaculus had put the expected date at May 2035. Mathematician Terence Tao said last month he expected the problem to fall to "a combination of humans and AI around 2050 or so."

news.title_zh: 斯坦福数学家完成黎曼猜想的形式化证明
news.summary_zh: 斯坦福大学数学家勒文特·阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge）通过Lean语言完成了黎曼猜想的证明，并经由Mathlib社区通过形式化验证确认无误
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】勒文特·阿尔珀格（Levent Alpöge，斯坦福大学数学家）在Lean与Mathlib形式化验证社区：完成黎曼猜想的形式化证明，并经多方独立运行代码验证通过
【起因与机理】作为数学界最重要的未决问题，其对于素数分布规律的解释具有基础性地位
【关键数据与实测】斯坦福数学家勒文特·阿尔珀格通过1700万行Lean代码破解黎曼猜想。
【各方立场与态度】解决时间远超Metaculus预测（2035年）及陶哲轩预判（2050年）。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Levent Alpöge, Mathematician at Stanford University: Completed the formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis verified by independent code execution
[Root Cause & Mechanism] It is a foundational problem regarding the distribution of prime numbers
[Key Technical Spec] Levent Alpöge solved the Riemann hypothesis using 17 million lines of Lean code.
[Key Position & Outlook] Solved much earlier than Metaculus predictions (2035) and Terence Tao's estimates (2050).

celebrity.title_zh:

假设一名代理已完成 500 项工作，成功率达 98%。这足以让某人放心地雇用它。

但是
celebrity.full_text_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai
celebrity.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理进化得越多，就越难知道它的声誉是否仍然意味着同样的事情。

我在探索 @termix_ai 和 ERC-8004 时一直在思考这个问题。

假设一名代理已完成 500 项工作，成功率达 98%。这足以让某人放心地雇用它。

但是，当开发人员更改其模型、替换其工具或完全重建其执行逻辑时会发生什么？

身份依然存在。声誉依然存在。但实际能力可能有所不同。

这是一个值得关注的问题。

ERC-8004 为代理提供了持久的身份和建立声誉的方法，但身份连续性并不一定意味着性能连续性。

为了使代理市场变得更加可靠，我认为用户应该能够看到

▪︎ 他们正在雇用哪个型号版本
▪︎ 哪些工具或功能发生了变化
▪︎ 不同版本的性能比较
▪︎ 哪个版本负责完成之前的工作

这与 TermiX 的 AACP 尤其相关，代理商可以在其中提供服务，
建立声誉并在链上进行交易。

如果代理的行为发生了根本性的变化，则代理不应自动继承旧版本获得的信任。

升级是必要的。更好的模型和新工具可以使代理人更有能力。

但声誉应该与代理人一起发展，而不是盲目追随其身份。

代理信任的未来可能不仅取决于代理是谁，还取决于哪个版本真正赢得了这种信任。 @termix_ai

an AI Agent needs more than intelligence to be useful in finance. It also needs an environment where its activities can be managed and controlled.

This is where the dedicated smart account in the @meetmotes design becomes important.

Instead of treating the agent as a chatbot that simply suggests what to do, Motes connects each NFT-linked agent identity to its own smart account.

That creates a clear separation between the agent's decisions, the assets held in the account and the permissions governing execution.

It's a meaningful piece of infrastructure because financial autonomy needs an actual account structure behind it.

The intelligence matters, but so does how it interacts with capital.

celebrity.title: What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts
celebrity.full_text_en:
What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts, or manually tweaking parameters?

That's the problem @quantpilotapp is working to solve.

@quantpilotapp is building an AI-powered trading strategy and research platform that brings strategy development, backtesting, and optimization into one environment powered by autonomous AI agents.

Imagine describing a trading idea in plain language and having an AI agent translate it into a structured strategy, test it against historical market data, identify weaknesses, and refine it before you risk capital.

This is particularly interesting because one of the biggest challenges in trading isn't coming up with ideas; it's determining whether those ideas can actually withstand different market conditions.

@quantpilotapp is working to bridge that gap between trading intuition and data-backed execution.

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Caddy 是一款人工智能助手，旨在帮助您通过消息传递管理日常任务。它与 Gmail、Google Calendar、Notion、Slack 和 Google Drive 等工具连接，将不同的工作流程整合到一处。

这是我最喜欢 Caddy 的一点：

➤ AI 支持的任务执行：它可以帮助起草电子邮件、安排事件和处理任务，而不是简单地建议您应该做什么。

➤ 主动帮助：每日摘要、提醒和跟进可帮助您掌握最新情况，而无需不断检查不同的应用程序。

➤ 连接的工作流程：其集成使跨多个平台管理信息变得更加容易，而无需在它们之间进行切换。

这是我的看法：

Caddy 的最大卖点是它的 Agentic AI 方法。它正在超越对话式人工智能，转向能够理解上下文并采取行动的代理。

然而，它仍处于公开测试阶段。在依赖它执行重要任务之前，我想进一步评估可靠性、隐私权限和长期定价。

还值得记住的是，好的人工智能产品需要的不仅仅是通过 SEO 和 GEO 获得可见性。一旦人们开始使用它们，它们就需要提供真正的价值。

罗
celebrity.full_text_en:
AN 18 YEAR OLD SAYS CLAUDE CODE PLAYED GTA 6 ALL NIGHT WHILE HE SLEPT AND MADE HIM $14,270.

His setup is one rule:

"Play all night. If you die, I cancel your $200 subscription."

He says the AI does the rest.

Robs.

Escapes.

Farms cash.

Records the clips.

Cuts them.

Captions them.

Posts them to TikTok, YouTube and Twitch.

His numbers:

1 night of heists = about 60 clips.

15M views = $14,270.

Zero editing.

Zero heists played by him.

Here's my take.

I don't buy the $14,270.

But I don't care about the money.

What matters is that a kid is threatening his AI with cancellation to make it play better.

And people are cheering.

We went from "AI will cure cancer" to "AI will grind my GTA heists" in one year.

Is this the future or the most cursed thing you've seen this week?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
一位 18 岁的年轻人说 Claude Code 在他睡觉的时候玩了整晚的 GTA 6，赚了 14,270 美元。

“玩一整晚。如果你死了，我就取消你 200 美元的订阅。”

他说人工智能会完成剩下的工作。

罗布斯。

逃脱。

农场现金。

记录剪辑。

切割它们。

为它们添加字幕。

将它们发布到 TikTok、YouTube 和 Twitch。

他的数字：

1 晚的抢劫 = 大约 60 个片段。

1500 万次浏览 = 14,270 美元。

零编辑。

他扮演的零抢劫。

这是我的看法。

我不买 14,270 美元。

但我不在乎钱。

重要的是，一个孩子正在威胁他的人工智能取消，以使其发挥得更好。

人们欢呼雀跃。

我们在一年内从“人工智能将治愈癌症”转变为“人工智能将粉碎我的 GTA 抢劫”。

这是未来还是本周你见过的最受诅咒的事情？

prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
人工智能代理进化得越多，就越难知道它的声誉是否仍然意味着同样的事情。

我在探索 @termix_ai 和 ERC-8004 时一直在思考这个问题。

假设一名代理已完成 500 项工作，成功率达 98%。这足以让某人放心地雇用它。

但是，当开发人员更改其模型、替换其工具或完全重建其执行逻辑时会发生什么？

身份依然存在。声誉依然存在。但实际能力可能有所不同。

这是一个值得关注的问题。

ERC-8004 为代理提供了持久的身份和建立声誉的方法，但身份连续性并不一定意味着性能连续性。

为了使代理市场变得更加可靠，我认为用户应该能够看到

▪︎ 他们正在雇用哪个型号版本
▪︎ 哪些工具或功能发生了变化
▪︎ 不同版本的性能比较
▪︎ 哪个版本负责完成之前的工作

这与 TermiX 的 AACP 尤其相关，代理商可以在其中提供服务，
建立声誉并在链上进行交易。

如果代理的行为发生了根本性的变化，则代理不应自动继承旧版本获得的信任。

升级是必要的。更好的模型和新工具可以使代理人更有能力。

但声誉应该与代理人一起发展，而不是盲目追随其身份。

代理信任的未来可能不仅取决于代理是谁，还取决于哪个版本真正赢得了这种信任。 @termix_ai

viral_posts.full_text_en:
What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts, or manually tweaking parameters?

That's the problem @quantpilotapp is working to solve.

@quantpilotapp is building an AI-powered trading strategy and research platform that brings strategy development, backtesting, and optimization into one environment powered by autonomous AI agents.

Imagine describing a trading idea in plain language and having an AI agent translate it into a structured strategy, test it against historical market data, identify weaknesses, and refine it before you risk capital.

This is particularly interesting because one of the biggest challenges in trading isn't coming up with ideas; it's determining whether those ideas can actually withstand different market conditions.

@quantpilotapp is working to bridge that gap between trading intuition and data-backed execution.

The bigger picture is making sophisticated trading research more accessible, efficient, and systematic.

AI in trading should be more than just automating decisions. It should help traders make better-informed ones.

That's the direction @quantpilotapp is exploring.

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在努力解决的问题。

@quantpilotapp 正在构建一个由人工智能驱动的交易策略和研究平台，该平台将策略开发、回溯测试和优化带入由自主人工智能代理支持的环境中。

@quantpilotapp 正在努力弥合交易直觉和数据支持执行之间的差距。

更大的前景是让复杂的交易研究变得更容易、更高效、更系统。

交易中的人工智能应该不仅仅是自动化决策。它应该可以帮助交易者做出更明智的交易。

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在探索的方向。

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Website: https://t.co/7U8jLFJWO8

𝐘𝐎𝐔𝐑 𝐀𝐈 𝐀𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐓 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐃𝐎 𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐍 𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐖𝐄𝐑𝐐𝐔𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒。

探索了@try_caddy，老实说，我认为这是使个人人工智能代理更有用的有趣的一步。

Caddy 是一款人工智能助手，旨在帮助您通过消息传递管理日常任务。它与 Gmail、Google Calendar、Notion、Slack 和 Google Drive 等工具连接，将不同的工作流程整合到一处。

这是我最喜欢 Caddy 的一点：

➤ AI 支持的任务执行：它可以帮助起草电子邮件、安排事件和处理任务，而不是简单地建议您应该做什么。

➤ 主动帮助：每日摘要、提醒和跟进可帮助您掌握最新情况，而无需不断检查不同的应用程序。

➤ 连接的工作流程：其集成使跨多个平台管理信息变得更加容易，而无需在它们之间进行切换。

这是我的看法：

Caddy 的最大卖点是它的 Agentic AI 方法。它正在超越对话式人工智能，转向能够理解上下文并采取行动的代理。

然而，它仍处于公开测试阶段。在依赖它执行重要任务之前，我想进一步评估可靠性、隐私权限和长期定价。

还值得记住的是，好的人工智能产品需要的不仅仅是通过 SEO 和 GEO 获得可见性。一旦人们开始使用它们，它们就需要提供真正的价值。
